en.title: Permutation Operation Count
en.description:
You are given a permutation p of 1..n. Repeatedly perform the operation where item i of the new array takes item p[i] of the old array. Find the minimum number of operations needed for any array of distinct elements to return to its original state, modulo 10^9+7.

The constraints are complete; the direction in which the permutation is applied does not affect the cycle lengths or the answer.

This site adds the standard input/output protocol; it does not mean the original site's function problem had this protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100000), and the second line contains the n numbers of p, a permutation of 1..n.
en.output: Output the minimum positive number of operations needed to restore the original array, modulo 1000000007.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the problem rules, approach, and proof.
hints: Decompose the permutation into disjoint cycles; the answer is the least common multiple of all cycle lengths.
